moat_against: Single-state, single-regulator (CPUC) concentration — no rate-case diversification
Regulators cap allowed returns; affordability pressure after double-digit rate increases
Catastrophic wildfire liability under inverse condemnation — $1.6B Eaton Fire settlement losses recorded, more probable
Capex permanently exceeds OCF — $37.5-40.6B 2026-2030 program funded with debt (net debt $37.84B)
moat_for: Exclusive regulated franchise — no competing wires provider in SCE's territory
Irreplaceable long-lived grid infrastructure with prohibitive replacement cost
Rate-base model: authorized returns underpin guided 5-7% core EPS growth 2025-2030
AB 1054 Wildfire Fund and self-insurance provide a structured wildfire recovery framework
moat_justification: SCE's exclusive California franchise, inelastic essential demand, and irreplaceable grid give a real regulated moat, but it is concentrated in one state and one regulator, allowed returns are capped, and California's inverse-condemnation wildfire liability sits outside the franchise's protection.
name: Edison International
one_liner: Regulated SCE franchise, moat 6/10, but Tier F on owner's earnings — conservative OE is negative in 0/5 last years because grid/wildfire capex exceeds OCF, so the OE DCF supports no hurdle at $55.68; F is a sector-model verdict, with Eaton Fire liability the real open risk.
